Service: MRI of the left knee without contrast (CPT 73721)
Provider: Riverside Orthopedic Associates

This is a formal internal appeal of the denial dated September 8, 2026 for an MRI of the left knee without contrast (CPT 73721). The plan denied the claim as not medically necessary, citing medical guideline MHP-MSK-014 and a requirement of at least six weeks of conservative treatment. I ask Meridian Health Plan of New York to overturn the denial and pay the claim. This appeal is filed within the time allowed [[cite:fed.internal_appeal.filing_window]].

sections.heading: Background
sections.text:
On August 20, 2026, I received an MRI of the left knee without contrast (CPT 73721) at Riverside Orthopedic Associates. The billed amount was $2,400. The plan paid $0. The amount listed as my responsibility is [ADD: patient responsibility amount from your EOB, if stated].

The denial notice dated September 8, 2026 states, using denial code 50: "The requested service is not medically necessary. Based on the clinical information submitted, our medical guideline MHP-MSK-014 (Advanced Imaging of the Knee) requires documentation of at least six weeks of conservative treatment."

My relevant history includes [ADD: your symptoms, when they started, and how they affect daily activities]. Before the MRI, I completed the following conservative treatment: [ADD: dates and details of physical therapy, rest, bracing, anti-inflammatory medication, injections, or other treatment, with dates].

sections.heading: Why the denial should be overturned
sections.text:
My treating provider at Riverside Orthopedic Associates ordered this MRI and considers it medically necessary. A supporting statement from the treating provider is enclosed or will follow: [ADD: treating provider's letter of medical necessity].

The denial appears to rest on missing documentation of conservative treatment rather than on a finding that the imaging had no clinical value. The records described above, together with the provider's statement, address that point directly and are submitted with this appeal.

Because this is a question of medical judgment, the appeal must be decided by a reviewer who was not involved in the first decision and who has appropriate clinical training and experience for knee and musculoskeletal care [[cite:fed.internal_appeal.independent_reviewer]]. I also ask the plan to provide the full text of guideline MHP-MSK-014 and the specific clinical criteria applied, which the notice must make available [[cite:fed.notice.required_content]] and which I may receive free of charge [[cite:fed.claim_file.free_copies]].

sections.heading: Requests
sections.text:
1. A complete copy of the claim file and every document, record, guideline, and protocol relied on in this decision, free of charge [[cite:fed.claim_file.free_copies]].

2. The specific clinical criteria and plan provision applied, including the full text of guideline MHP-MSK-014, and the name, specialty, and credentials of the reviewer who made the decision [[cite:fed.notice.required_content]] [[cite:fed.internal_appeal.independent_reviewer]].

3. A written decision within the time frame required for a post-service appeal [[cite:fed.internal_appeal.decision_windows]], and under New York rules for utilization review appeals [[cite:ny.internal_appeal.deemed_reversal]].

4. Review by a health professional with training and experience in orthopedics or musculoskeletal imaging, with no deference given to the original decision [[cite:fed.internal_appeal.independent_reviewer]].

5. A written explanation of what conservative treatment documentation the plan found missing, and consideration of the records enclosed with this appeal [[cite:fed.notice.required_content]].

I can be reached at [ADD: your phone number] or [ADD: your email address]. If Meridian Health Plan of New York upholds the denial, I reserve the right to request an independent external review [[cite:fed.external_review.filing_window]] or a New York State external appeal with the Department of Financial Services, which covers medical necessity denials [[cite:ny.external_appeal.scope]] [[cite:ny.external_appeal.filing_window]]. My employer plan may be self-funded, in which case the federal external review route applies [[cite:fed.erisa.self_funded_route]].

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,
[ADD: your full name]
[ADD: your signature]
